key_insight: Entropically stabilized Neural Discrete Equilibrium (NeurDE) enables stable, long-time turbulent-flow emulation on extremely coarse grids by reinforcing physical dissipation.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support efficient coarse-grid turbulence forecasting while reducing instability from unresolved small-scale dynamics.
method: Use NeurDE to emulate fluid dynamics on coarse grids.
Control entropy dynamics to reinforce the system’s dissipative mechanism.
Suppress instability associated with unresolved frequencies and grid-scale aliasing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stable rollouts over thousands of forecasting steps at Re = 100,000 on grids as coarse as 16×16, with stability sometimes exceeding the stabilized data-generation solver.
watch_item: Long-time stability alone does not establish accuracy of turbulent statistics; the abstract does not quantify that fidelity.
paper_title: Learning the Entropic Relaxation: Stable Coarse-Grid Emulation with Neural Discrete Equilibrium
